```{r functions}
source("catHeader.R")


investigate_raw_maps <- function(to_plot, request){
    request <- eval(request)
    request <- quo_name(enquo(request))
    
    raw_map(data = to_plot[[request]], 
            well = to_plot$well, 
            plate = 96) + labs(title = request)
}


investigate_b_maps <- function(to_plot, request){
    request <- eval(request)
    request <- quo_name(enquo(request))
    
    b_map(data = to_plot[[request]], 
          well = to_plot$well, 
          plate = 96) + labs(title = request)
}

```

## Importing data

```{r import}
# the plate map

pilot_map <- fread("AAVS1_experiment_genekey.csv") %>% 
    dplyr::rename(gene = cmpdname)


# the plates
plate_1 <- fread("AAVS1_imaging_output.txt", skip = 1) %>% 
    mutate(well = paste0(LETTERS[Row], sprintf("%02d", Column))) %>% 
    filter(!Row %in% c(1, 8) & !Column %in% c(1, 12)) %>%  # removing the 1st outer edge because it is empty
    merge(., pilot_map, by = "well")



```

### Feature breakdown, raw values, plate 1 {.tabset .tabset-pills}

For a better picture of the data distribution, instead of just counts.

```{r rawbreakdown, results='asis', echo=FALSE}

pltting_list <- colnames(plate_1) #get list of variables to plot

pltting_list <-  pltting_list[! pltting_list %in% c("Row", "Column", "well", "gene")] #remove cluster and eid from list of names

plot_compile <- list() #start an empty list for storing the plots

for (i in seq_along(pltting_list)) { # loop across the list of variables to plot
    
    name <- paste0(pltting_list[i]) #make names for each plot
    plot_compile[[name]] <- investigate_raw_maps(to_plot = plate_1, #store in each unique name this following ggplot
                                                 request = pltting_list[i])
    
}

for (j in seq_along(plot_compile)) { # loop across list of plots
    
    tmp <- plot_compile[[j]] # store temporarily each ggplot
    
    catHeader(pltting_list[j], 4) #for tabs. comment out to see all at once
    
    print(tmp) #print each ggplot
    
}

```

### Power calculations iteration function
```{r powercalcfunc}

no_NTCs <- 12

no_genes <- 12

no_control_wells <- 36

no_wells_compound <- 3


### turn into function


PowerCalc <- function(variables_of_interest, gene_of_interest, no_control_wells, no_wells_compound, no_NTCs, no_genes){
    
    # NTC mean and stdev across all plates
    mean_NTC_power <- mean(big_plate_additional_factors[[variables_of_interest]][str_detect(big_plate_additional_factors$gene, "NTC")])
    stdev_NTC_power <- sd(big_plate_additional_factors[[variables_of_interest]][str_detect(big_plate_additional_factors$gene, "NTC")])
    
    
    # gene mean and stdev across all plates
    mean_gene_power <- mean(big_plate_additional_factors[[variables_of_interest]][str_detect(big_plate_additional_factors$gene, gene_of_interest)])
    stdev_gene_power <- sd(big_plate_additional_factors[[variables_of_interest]][str_detect(big_plate_additional_factors$gene, gene_of_interest)])
    
    #pooled sd
    pooled_sd <- sqrt( (((no_NTCs - 1)*(stdev_NTC_power^2)) + ((no_genes - 1)*(stdev_gene_power^2)))/(no_NTCs+no_genes-2))
    
    #final power calc
    power_equiv <- (qnorm(0.8) + qnorm(0.95))*(pooled_sd * sqrt((1/no_control_wells) + (1/no_wells_compound)))/abs(mean_NTC_power - mean_gene_power)
    
    # print answer
    print(power_equiv)
    
}


### turn into iterative function

variables_of_interest <- c(colnames(big_plate_additional_factors))[13]
genes_of_interest <- c(unique(big_plate_additional_factors$gene)) # c("IRS1", "PTEN")
results <- vector("list", length(genes_of_interest))

for (i in seq_along(genes_of_interest)) {
    
    temp_gene <- genes_of_interest[i]
    
    temp_power <- PowerCalc(variables_of_interest, temp_gene, no_control_wells = 135, no_wells_compound = 9, no_NTCs, no_genes)
    
    # Add to list
    
    results[[i]] <- list(gene = temp_gene, power = temp_power)
    
}

power_dataframe <- bind_rows(results)

ggplot(power_dataframe, mapping = aes(x = gene, y = power))+
    geom_point()+
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.3, linetype = 2)+
    theme_minimal()+
    scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2))+
    labs(title = paste0("Power calculations for ", variables_of_interest),
         subtitle = "For n = 9")+
    ylim(0,1)


### not sure these are the right plots to be making lol

```

### Effect sizes iteration
```{r iteration}


variables_of_interest <- setdiff(colnames(big_plate_additional_factors), c("well","Row","Column","gene"))

for (temp_var in variables_of_interest) {
    
    
    mean_NTC_p1 <- mean(big_plate_additional_factors[[temp_var]][str_detect(big_plate_additional_factors$gene, "NTC")])
    
    
    stdev_p1 <- sd(big_plate_additional_factors[[temp_var]])
    
    
    
    big_plate_effect_sizes <- big_plate_additional_factors %>% 
        mutate(
            nuclei_count_z_score =((.data[[temp_var]]-mean_NTC_p1)/stdev_p1),
            sigma_z_score =  sd(nuclei_count_z_score[str_detect(gene, "NTC")]),
            nuclei_count_effect_size = (nuclei_count_z_score/sigma_z_score)
        )
    
    big_plate_effect_sizes <- big_plate_additional_factors %>%
        mutate(
            z_score_col = ((.data[[temp_var]] - mean_NTC_p1) / stdev_p1)
        )
    
    
    # Calculate sigma_z_score using the new z-score column
    sigma_z_score <- sd(big_plate_effect_sizes$z_score_col[str_detect(big_plate_effect_sizes$gene, "NTC")])
    
    # Add effect size column
    big_plate_effect_sizes <- big_plate_effect_sizes %>%
        mutate(
            effect_size = z_score_col/sigma_z_score
        )
    
    ggplot(big_plate_effect_sizes, mapping = aes(x = gene, y = effect_size)) + 
        geom_boxplot()+
        scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2))+
        theme_minimal()+
        ggtitle(paste0(temp_var, " effect size")) -> p
    
    print(p)
    
    
    
}



```

```{r cohensd}

library(effsize)

treatment = rnorm(100,mean=10)
control = rnorm(100,mean=12)
d = (c(treatment,control))
f = rep(c("Treatment","Control"),each=100)
## compute Cohen's d
## treatment and control
cohen.d(treatment,control)
## data and factor
cohen.d(d,f)
## formula interface
cohen.d(d ~ f)
```

```{r asca}


library(multiblock)


# Load candies data
data(candies)

# Basic ASCA model with two factors
mod <- asca(assessment ~ candy + assessor, data=candies)
print(mod)

# ASCA model with interaction
mod <- asca(assessment ~ candy * assessor, data=candies)
print(mod)

# Result plotting for first factor
loadingplot(mod, scatter=TRUE, labels="names")
scoreplot(mod)
# No backprojection
scoreplot(mod, projections=FALSE)
# Spider plot
scoreplot(mod, spider=TRUE)

# asca vs pcanova vs apca

# Basic PC-ANOVA model with two factors, cross-validated opt. of #components
mod <- pcanova(assessment ~ candy + assessor, data = candies)
print(mod)

# Tukey group letters for 'candy' per component
lapply(mod$models, function(x)
       mixlm::cld(mixlm::simple.glht(x,
                                     effect = "candy")))

# Result plotting
loadingplot(mod, scatter=TRUE, labels="names")
scoreplot(mod)
```
